properties.name: A near-match at a prescribed layer of the capture loop is reported, not refused
properties.rationale:
Anthony's word, 2026-08-31, on the count the 2026-08-29 repair named as its own reopening condition: "Nobody has counted how often a cross-type hit IS a real duplicate." The count is `fact:twelve-near-match-refusals-across-two-designs-and-not-one-was-a-duplicate` — 12 field refusals across two designs whose sessions could not see each other, 12 judged distinct, 0 duplicates, plus 3 incurred by the triage session itself while writing the decision that acts on it.

⭐ WHY THE FALSE-POSITIVE RATE WAS NOT THE DECIDING ARGUMENT. The silent miss that option ① was rejected to avoid had ALREADY ARRIVED by another route: bhome, at its eighth refusal, "started passing `distinct_from` pre-emptively", and concluded that a guard routinely pre-empted has stopped being a check. Doing nothing preserved the appearance of a check and none of its effect.

🛑 THE SET IS THE PAIRS WITH EVIDENCE, NOT EVERY PAIR THAT COULD BE ARGUED FOR. Requirement↔Component is plausibly a layer pair and is deliberately absent — nobody has measured it, and adding it would be the same unmeasured assumption the 2026-08-29 repair refused to make in the other direction.

Pinned by five tests written first and OBSERVED FAILING in the right split: the three that must change failed, and the two counterweights — a same-type duplicate still refused, an unmeasured cross-type pair still refused with the layer wording — passed against the unfixed code, which is what shows the tests discriminate rather than merely accepting the new behaviour.

📌 STILL OPEN, and not fixed here: the refusal returns only ONE LAYER of the near-match set, so `distinct_from` cannot be answered in one call. Measured this session (three attempts, the full node body re-sent each time). It is a defect independent of how the guard is tuned and now fires far less often, but it is not gone.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
`refuse_unless_deliberate` drops prescribed-layer matches before deciding whether to refuse. `PRESCRIBED_LAYER_PAIRS` in capture.rs holds the pairs with evidence behind them — Requirement↔Capability, ChangeEvent↔{Requirement,Decision,Capability}, Decision↔{Capability,Component}, TemporalFact↔Decision — matched in either direction. One SAME-TYPE exemption is keyed on `kind` rather than type: a Decision created against an `exploratory` Decision is the brainstorm skill's promotion step, so `NearMatch` gained an optional `kind`, read only for Decisions and `None` on a failed lookup (the conservative direction — a read error can cost a round trip, never a silent suppression).

🛑 THE REFUSAL IS SUPPRESSED; THE REPORT IS NOT. A prescribed-layer match still comes back in `search_first.near_matches` exactly as before, so the caller still sees what it matched and a later reader can still find it. That is the difference between narrowing a guard and blinding it, and a test asserts it — without that assertion this change would be indistinguishable from deleting the check.

Option ② from 2026-08-29 survives underneath: an UNMEASURED cross-type pair still refuses, and still with the layer wording.
